item.title: Season 12 Phase 4 Vote, and What's Next For Playoffs Qualification
item.description:
Hello everyone! Earlier this season, we announced that the Season 12 phase point system will feature some changes from previous seasons. Phases 1 and 3 would still use the traditional end-of-phase Elo phase point system, phase 2 would use a new phase-peak Elo phase point system, and the community would choose between these two systems to use in phase 4 through a community poll.

Starting on 2026-11-23 00:00 UTC until 2026-11-28 00:00 UTC, all players with a Season 12 peak Elo at or above 1800 will have the option to vote in the community poll. The poll itself will just be a Google Form, posted in the MCSR Ranked Discord server. Shortly after the poll closes, the anonymized results will be published, and whichever system has more votes will be used for phase 4.

📝 Note

If you wish to submit a response without using the Google Form, or want to query the state of or change your response, please open a ticket in the MCSR Ranked Discord server. Invalid or fraudulent responses will be scanned for and culled. Some players may be given early access to submit their responses.

The History of The Phase Point System

Prior to Season 4, the top 8 players on the leaderboard at the end of each season would qualify directly to the Playoffs bracket. This system was simple, but flawed. Elo and leaderboard positions were (and still are) quite volatile, so a single snapshot of the leaderboard didn’t always provide an accurate ranking of the best players. The phase point system was introduced to fix this issue, among a few others.

Since Season 5, each season has been split into four, month long phases.1 At the end of each phase, the top 100 players on the leaderboard would receive phase points, with higher ranking players earning significantly more phase points. At the end of the season, the top 12 players based on phase points would qualify for the Playoffs bracket. Essentially, this system averages out top ranked players’ leaderboard positions over a season, meaning Playoffs qualification was no longer based on a single snapshot of the volatile Elo leaderboard.

Other than a few tweaks over the years, the phase point system has remained very similar to its original implementation in Season 4. In this time though, cracks have been starting to show. For example, like how the pre-Season 4 system only took a single snapshot of the leaderboard each season, the phase point system only takes four snapshots, which isn’t much better. Top players often lose motivation to play at the start of each phase, or don’t queue later in the phase to avoid the risk of losing.

A Solution: Phase-Peak Elo

A popular solution to the problems with this phase point system was proposed by the community: instead of awarding phase points based on end-of-phase Elo, award them based on the highest Elo rating achieved during the phase, or phase-peak Elo. The phase-peak system promised to fix many issues of the end-of-phase system for several reasons. First and foremost, the phase-peak system doesn’t just look at a few snapshots of the volatile leaderboard since players can reach a peak Elo at any point in the phase. Second, once a player is below their phase-peak Elo, losing an individual match doesn’t directly result in earning less phase points for the phase, which removes much of the reason why top players may choose not to queue later in the phase.

For Season 12, we were hesitant to adopt the phase-peak system fully. Highly ranked players that are no longer attempting to set a new phase-peak Elo do not have Playoffs qualification as an incentive to win their matches, but they are still able to queue players that do have that incentive. Having “serious” players queue against “non-serious” players is not a problem unique to the phase-peak system, but it makes it far more obvious when it occurs. This issue, among a few others, combined with the fact that it was simply a new system that could have unknown issues, was enough to dissuade us from fully committing to the phase-peak system for Season 12. We still wanted to mix things up though, and this idea was popular, hence our decision to try it out just for phase 2, and potentially phase 4. We would be the first to admit that this alternating system isn’t ideal, but we wanted to try something new.

As for the community vote: we didn’t want to commit to using the phase-peak system for phase 4, in case it didn’t work out in phase 2, and giving the community the choice to pick their preferred system seemed fitting. Originally, the poll was going to be open to all Ranked players, but this was clearly unpopular with the community, per feedback and discussion following the initial announcement. So, we’ve changed course to only allow players with some likelihood to earn phase points to participate, which we’ve decided to be a Season 12 peak Elo of 1800 or higher.

The Future of Playoffs Formats

The phase-peak system was somewhat successful in phase 2, but it also just didn’t change much compared to the flawed end-of-phase system. Ultimately, both these systems are flawed for the same reason: in-season Ranked matches are the primary way to qualify for Playoffs, but these matches aren’t held to nearly the same standard as Playoffs matches (by the players, community, and Ranked staff). Of course people care less about a random Ranked queue than a Playoffs match, but this frequently leads to anti-competitive or just noncompetitive behavior directly influencing who qualifies for Playoffs.

To be clear, I don’t think the existing systems qualify the “wrong” players, in fact I think the existing qualification systems have done an excellent job at selecting the most deserving and skilled players. But simply selecting the best players is not the only goal of the Playoffs qualification system, or even Playoffs as a whole. Qualifying to Playoffs is also supposed to be a goal for the most ambitious Ranked players to strive for, and an incentive to continue improving at speedrunning Minecraft. For this to be the case though, the journey to achieve that goal needs to be fun and rewarding. It should feel fair and objective, and not unnecessarily tedious. It should be entertaining to viewers to watch and engage with a player’s journey to qualify, which necessitates that the player is having fun themselves.

With all that being said, our intention for the Season 13 Playoffs qualification format is for it to be event based, rather than leaderboard based. Throughout the season, there will be several qualification events, and the top performers in these events are who qualify to Playoffs. There will likely still be some reliance on the leaderboard, for example it’s possible that only players above a certain place on the leaderboard will be eligible to participate in a qualification event, or these may be seeded using in-season Elo. But the goal is that tournaments host the last few matches that carry the weight of Playoffs qualification, not just random in-season Ranked queues.

Expect another blog post in the coming weeks talking more about the upcoming Playoffs qualification changes.

Thank you for reading,

-r0hkx

  1. Season 4 only had three phases, but was otherwise used a very similar system compared to Season 5. ↩︎

item.title: Mod Update - v6.0.5 Changelog
item.description:
Winter is coming! So, we’ve changed the theme of ranked as well!
Also The Frostbite Invitational is very soon at Twitchcon San Diego 2026! Don’t forget to watch this special event!

Changes

  • New Winter Theme!
    • You can toggle off this theme in Ranked Settings
  • Woodlight Standardization is now enabled in Private room and Casual Mode by default
    • We plan to apply this standardization in Ranked Mode Season 13 after current playtesting.
  • MCSR Ranked will no longer launch without certain legal launchers.
    • This change is to follow the SR.C leaderboard rules and reduce cheating methods.
    • You can check all the whitelisted launchers in here (A.1.1)
  • Added reduced live replay delay option in RSA for private rooms
  • Added auto pie chart and new UI for pie chart in replays
  • Many bug fixes and small improvements in replay

Bug Reports

Please join our Discord Server to report any issues!

item.title: Rebuild the Core - Progress on the Server Rewrite
item.description:
Hello, everyone! We’re so glad with finally I can post about this publicly.
We know that content updates have been somewhat lacking aside from the recent replay updates, and we believe you have noticed this as well.

In the background, We’ve been putting so much effort into reinsfrastructuring the entire MCSR Ranked backend(the server).
Now, we will explain why we have to do that, what’s going to be changed, and when it will happen.

Problems of current server infrastructure

The backend code for MCSR Ranked began to be rewritten in late 2022. Wow, it’s already been nearly 4 years.
During this process, I (RedLime) wrote 99% of the backend code, and you might be surprised, this was my first attempt at a WebSocket project.
In short, before starting this project, I had absolutely no idea how WebSocket worked, and I literally started learning about it as I began the project.
I also lacked a significant amount of technical knowledge regarding various backends.

However, with a lot of help of Google search, I made the first version of the backend, and surprisingly, the server started working!
But, this initial backend was not designed to accommodate thousands of players playing simultaneously.
Because We never even imagined that the project would eventually reach thousands of concurrent users. It was literally our passion project.

Fast forward some years later, several issues began to surface.
From 2023 to 2024, there were a few performance issues on the server, but since these were primarily database optimization problems, they could be fixed easily. However, from late 2025 to early 2026, a massive influx of players began all at once due to the Tubbo’s Midoffs and spectacular plays of Ludwig. The average number of concurrent users jumped more than 10x in an instant, which was completely unexpected. As a result, various structural problems with the backend design began to be discovered.

Memory usage and performance with Database

We had used a No-SQL database. because the initial MCSR Ranked backend required various changes, which facilitates data structure modifications.
However, at this point, the database’s structure become relatively stabilized, and various problems also arised due to the inherent limitations of No-SQL.
Memory usages and performance degration were particularly severe. Specifically, as the number of matches and users increased, memory began to occupy up to 50% of the current server’s total memory, and is still increasing.
And also, due to the limit of No-SQL, performance lags significantly when using queries that link multiple tables for analysis. Consequently, it was difficult to implement various analytical functions within the server.
This naturally became a major obstacle to adding new features to the server and established a critical challenge that needed to be resolved.

Everything is in single core/process

Similarly, another issue has appeared that was not a problem in the past but has emerged as the number of users increased.
Currently, the MCSR Ranked backend bundles all services into a single process. This includes the game server, API, Discord bot, website proxy, and other services.
Therefore, if even one of these elements has a significant heavy performance load or an error that causes the process to crash, the entire server crashes with it.

Yes, the situations shown in these videos were caused precisely by this problem.

Another problem is that since all of this works within a single process, the server’s full CPU performance cannot be utilized. Although the server currently has multiple cores, the game server process was using only a single core. This resulted in a waste of performance.
Fortunately, since the Database and proxy processing systems were using multiple cores, it was not a complete waste.

Hard to hotfix for specific element

This issue is directly related to the single process problem mentioned above.
If a minor issue occurred in the server logic requiring a hotfix, or if changes were needed to the API, the entire server had to be restarted unconditionally. This was the case even for a single line of code change.

This is important because it means that any ongoing Ranked Mode gameplay must also be suspended. Basically, it takes at least an hour to inspect and restart the entire server. We have to wait for ongoing matches to finish, apply the patch, and then perform a final check of the changes.
While this would be perfectly reasonable for large-scale updates, the same steps are required even to apply a single line of code change.
Since such long downtime is not ideal, a method was needed to manage each process more efficiently.

The new infrastructure

To resolve all these issues and ensure scalability to accommodate more players in the future, we have built a new server infrastructure.

We have separated each major feature into a separate process: The game server, API, and Discord bot, to ensure that applying changes does not affect other services.
Furthermore, because the processes are separated, each service can utilize an entire single core, which grants significantly more CPU performance available to the service.

Additionally, the API and Game Server can also be split into multiple processes. This allows us to handle increased demand in the future by simply adding more processes, while also making the deployment of updates much easier.
In particular, if changes are required for the Game Server, we create a new process with the updated changes and prevent access to the existing process, enabling the changes to be applied to players sequentially.

The database has also been migrated to a SQL-based architecture. This allows for more efficient memory usage, smaller data sizes, and improved performance.
While it is difficult to go into specific details about this, just know a lot of effort has been put into it. 🫠

Future Plans & New Features

In fact, We’ve already started the private test with this new server infrastructure! This update is planned around the near future if we don’t have any major issue while in the private testing phase, and we expect it around this December or start of Season 13!

Also, we’ve implemented some new features for testing the new server performance already:

  • Match API bulk files for download and every match API data in a specific season.
  • Fastest time leaderboard with Country filter.

After this update, we will start to work on some wanted features:

  • Pronouns
  • New Seed Rush Mode
  • Notification of Report Reviewed
  • Cosmetics Update

Some tasks applied only in the client, such as standardization or UI rework among other things, haven’t been included in this list. Of course, those will also be worked on.

Postscript

We would like to take this opportunity to apologize for the updates that have been delayed due to the work on this massive undertaking.
The features mentioned earlier will be implemented after the deployment of the server rewrite, and we look forward to introducing even more contents to MCSR Ranked in 2027.
Thank you for your patience.

I would also like to give thanks to Roco and eva (xyzeva) for their contributions to this update.
With Eva, she provided the concepts and demo architecture for this new infrastructure. Without her, this project wouldn’t have been possible.
Roco also helped an entire rewrite process, with her efforts, we are on track to complete this work within this year.

Discussion

Feel free to discuss about this update in our Discord Server!

Thank you everyone for your suggestions or feedback. :)

item.title: Mod Update - v6.0.4 Changelog
item.description:
We are still fixing some issues with replay update! But we’ve added an option that many players has requested!
Checkout the entire Replay v3.0 update changelog in This Post!
And still, we are getting feedback/suggestions with the new replay update! Please don’t forget to join our Discord Server!

Changes

  • Added Auto open containers option in replay.
    • It does open/close the containers(e.g. inventory, crafting table and chests) in player cam mode.
    • It is disabled by default, you can enable it on replay settings.
  • Fixed issues with pearl hangs, and added a marker in replays.
  • Fixed an issue with dragon death sound.
  • You can rebind with mouse buttons for replay/ranked controls binding.
  • Fixed an issue where dragon fly away height info in replay was incorrect.
    • Also changed the rendering of dragon target distance.
  • Some bug fixes in replay.

Bug Reports

Please join our Discord Server to report any issues!

item.title: Mod Update - v6.0.3 Changelog
item.description:
We are fixing some issues, and there’s noticeable change with the blind portal behavior.
Checkout the entire Replay v3.0 update changelog in This Post!
And also, we are getting feedback/suggestions with the new replay update! Please don’t forget to join our Discord Server!

Changes

  • Blind portals generated in ocean biomes will no longer be fixed at Y-70.
    • We already had logic to generate blind portals on the surface. However, a side effect of this logic was that blind portals generated in ocean biomes would always spawn at Y-70. After reviewing the code, we realized that this is different from vanilla behavior, so we fixed it.
    • Blind portals can now generate at much higher(like as vanilla). As a result, it will be difficult to reach without throwing ender pearls or placing blocks to climb up.
  • Fixed some replay bugs.

Bug Reports

Please join our Discord Server to report any issues!

item.title: Mod Update - v6.0.0 Changelogs
item.description:
This update focuses on the new replay system, along with some smaller changes.
We’re also collecting feedback and suggestions! Join our Discord Server!

Changes

  • Replay v3.0 Update
    • This update brings a complete overhaul to the replay system, with lots of new features, bug fixes, QOL improvements and more. Not to mention a complete tutorial to get you acquainted!
    • Summary of all the replay changes:
      • New replay UI & controls
      • Replay tutorial
      • First-person POV
      • Player health, hunger, breath, inventory & more stats
      • Visualize mob/player pathing
      • Splits viewer, navigation & alignment
      • Piglin trades stat screen
      • X-ray spawners/chests/gold blocks
      • Pie chart recording
      • Player UI interaction recording
      • Looted/unlooted toggle for chests
      • New timeline icons (by ollie)
      • And more!
  • Fixed an issue where ocean seed types would sometimes have both a shipwreck and buried treasure at spawn.
  • All strongholds now generate with the same rooms and layout, and still have the same number of eyes.
    • However, they can still be affected by other generated structures, such as caves, dungeons and mineshafts. We are looking into a way to fix this in the future.
  • Added more splash texts.

Bug Reports

Please join our Discord Server to report any issues!

item.title: Mod Update - v5.8.25 Changelogs
item.description:
This is the first public changelogs in this blog! We are so glad with it 😊
Anyways, this update isn’t big update. but also, this is preparation for the Replay v3.0 Update. Focused on server storage for replays especially.

Changes

  • Replay storage update
    • As we’ve mentioned in the last maintenance announcement, We’ve changed a lot of backend stuffs for the replay storage, Due to this change, every past match replays are deleted from the server. However, you can still access on Weekly Race replays.
    • Replay expiration time has been extended from 3 days to 7 days.
    • Ranked mode match replays in the Top 50 record leaderboard of each season will now be stored as no expiration time.
    • You can no longer download or watch more than 5 replays per minute
  • Updated tab selections in ranked settings screen.
  • Added more splash texts.

Bug Reports

Please join our Discord Server to report any issues!
